note: Byte-immutable once committed, so the tool_set_sha256 embedded in already-recorded runs still verifies. A changed spec goes in a new tools.v{n+1}.json rather than editing this file, which is the device configs/today.json already uses.

bioactivity.prior_binders.name: bioactivity.prior_binders
bioactivity.prior_binders.summary: Prior bioactivities, assay formats and public mutational landscapes for one protein.
bioactivity.prior_binders.description: Queries ChEMBL for recorded bioactivities against a target accession, IEDB for mapped epitopes, and MaveDB for deep mutational scanning datasets, then reports what each lane found and which lanes could not be reached. Peptide and macrocycle-shaped molecules are separated from small molecules, because the question this project asks of precedent is narrow: not whether anything has ever bound the target, but whether anything of the molecule class under development has.

parameters.name: accession
parameters.meaning: UniProt accession the lanes are keyed on.

parameters.name: target_name
parameters.meaning: A name used where a lane cannot be queried by accession, or absent.

parameters.name: max_molecules
parameters.meaning: How many bioactivity records to retrieve and shape-classify.

parameters.name: record
parameters.meaning: Whether the function writes its own artifact. An episode passes False.

returns: Bioactivity counts and assay formats, split by molecule shape.
Mapped epitopes, where any were found.
Public mutational-scanning datasets naming this protein.
What each lane's return does and does not license per axis, stated in the payload so a count cannot travel without it.
The earliest year any retrieved record was published.
Lanes that could not be reached, kept apart from lanes that returned nothing. An unreached source is not an absence of evidence.
Identity of the payload with timestamps stripped.
Host, commit and time, from common.provenance.

failures.symptom: a lane could not be reached
failures.cause: Three independent public endpoints. One being unavailable is recorded in `lanes_unavailable` rather than raised, because the other two still answer and an unreached lane must not read as an empty one.

failures.symptom: urllib.error.HTTPError from the ChEMBL, IEDB or MaveDB host
failures.cause: Public keyless endpoints. Raised when the integrated query itself fails rather than one lane.

bioactivity.prior_binders.citation: The ChEMBL activity and assay identifiers, the IEDB epitope identifiers and the MaveDB dataset accessions, with the year each was published. A row count with no identifiers is not a cited claim.
bioactivity.prior_binders.warning: A row in a bioactivity database is not an assay you can run, and a count of them is not an available assay. A small-molecule bioactivity is also not precedent for a macrocycle, which is why the shapes are separated rather than totalled.

chemistry.library_spec.name: chemistry.library_spec
chemistry.library_spec.summary: Define a focused thioether-macrocycle library over a randomised region.
chemistry.library_spec.description: Returns a library definition: a fixed chloroacetyl initiator, a randomised region of the given length bounds, a downstream cysteine closure, and the elongator alphabet implied by the requested monomer classes. It defines a library and does not synthesise, screen or score one, and the theoretical diversity it reports is a count of sequences the definition admits rather than a prediction that any of them bind.

parameters.name: initiator
parameters.meaning: Chloroacetyl initiator, which must be one the chemistry module registers.

parameters.name: random_region
parameters.meaning: Inclusive (low, high) length bounds for the randomised region.

parameters.name: elongator_classes
parameters.meaning: Monomer classes admitted into the elongator alphabet.

returns: The residue that closes the macrocycle.
Monomer codes the region draws from.
Sequences the definition admits. Not a library that exists, and not a count of anything measured.

failures.symptom: '<name>' is not a registered chloroacetyl initiator
failures.cause: The initiator is validated against the chemistry module's own table, which is narrower than the set of strings the schema admits.
The bounds must satisfy 1 <= low <= high, which a JSON schema cannot express portably, so the function enforces it.
Every requested monomer class was unknown, leaving nothing to draw from.

chemistry.library_spec.citation: A library definition is a design choice, not a cited claim, and cannot substantiate a dossier axis on its own.
chemistry.library_spec.warning: Theoretical diversity is a combinatorial count over the definition. It is not a synthesised library, not a screened one, and no macrocycle has been measured anywhere in this repository.

families.entries.name: families.entries
families.entries.summary: Family, domain and site assignments claiming one protein, with residue ranges.
families.entries.description: Resolves InterPro's integrated entries for a protein accession and returns each family, domain and functional site with the member database that asserted it, its accession, and the residue ranges it covers. The residue ranges are the point: they turn a claim about a protein into a claim about a site, which is what a structural lookup and a binder both need. Also returns a literature query key, which is how a novel target reaches a literature that has never heard of it.

parameters.name: accession
parameters.meaning: UniProt accession whose entries are resolved, or the caller's label when a sequence is supplied instead.

parameters.name: sequence
parameters.meaning: Amino-acid sequence to scan when no accession resolves, or empty.

parameters.name: include_predicted
parameters.meaning: Whether to include assignments from predicted rather than curated member databases.

parameters.name: max_families
parameters.meaning: How many assignments to return.

parameters.name: record
parameters.meaning: Whether the function writes its own artifact. An episode passes False.

returns: Family and domain assignments, each with its member database, accession, name and residue ranges.
Assignments grouped by what kind of claim each is.
Site-level assignments where any were made.
The family name or accession best suited to a literature query, which is the route that works when the target itself is unpublished.
How many assignments of each kind were returned.
Databases that returned nothing, kept apart from databases that were not reached, because a silent absence and an unreached source are different.
The organism the accession belongs to.
Identity of the payload with timestamps stripped.
Host, commit and time, from common.provenance.

failures.cause: A public keyless endpoint. A 404 on one member database is recorded as an absence rather than raised, because a protein with no entry in one database is the ordinary case; an error on the integrated endpoint raises.

families.entries.citation: The InterPro entry accessions, the member databases that asserted them and their releases. A family name with no entry accession is not a cited claim.
families.entries.warning: A family assignment is an annotation transferred from relatives and is never a measurement on this pathogen. Conservation across curated database entries is also not conservation across circulating strains, and the two are routinely conflated.

geometry.surface_markers.name: geometry.surface_markers
geometry.surface_markers.summary: Macrocycle-shaped surface markers for one protein accession, from deposited structures.
geometry.surface_markers.description: Resolves the best-resolution deposited chains for a UniProt accession, optionally restricted to a residue interval, and computes per-structure solvent accessibility with freesasa. Reports the largest contiguous exposed hydrophobic patch as a median over up to five structures of the same domain, with the minimum, maximum and spread beside it, plus the exposed fraction, the patch as a share of total surface, and the count of N-linked glycosylation sequons within glycan reach of the patch. The markers are interface-shaped rather than pocket-shaped on purpose: a small-molecule druggability score is calibrated on deep enclosed cavities and a macrocycle binds the opposite, so on pocket depth the main protease outscores the spike receptor-binding domain, which is correct for a small molecule and backwards here. It measures a surface and predicts no affinity.

parameters.name: accession
parameters.meaning: Reviewed UniProt accession whose best deposited chains are measured.

parameters.name: interval
parameters.meaning: Residue interval to restrict the representative-structure choice to, or absent for the whole chain.

parameters.name: replicates
parameters.meaning: How many structures of the same domain to measure before taking the median.

returns: Median largest contiguous exposed hydrophobic patch, square angstroms. A macrocyclic peptide buries roughly 400 to 800 on binding.
Max minus min. A patch of 600 give or take 40 is a different claim from 600 give or take 300, and one structure is one sample of an ensemble.
Share of residues at or above the exposure cut.
The patch as a share of total surface, which separates one large contiguous site from a large protein carrying many small ones.
N-linked sequons within glycan reach of the patch. The honest counterweight on a viral surface protein: a conserved exposed patch covered in glycan is not the opportunity its area suggests.

One stated, unfitted weighting of the markers for a macrocycle. Not fitted, because there is no labelled set of macrocycle-amenable targets to fit against and building one from the targets under test is circular.
How many structures the median is over.

Earliest deposition date among the structures measured, or absent when none could be resolved. When this claim became knowable -- a patch is evidence from the day the coordinates showing it were deposited, not from the day it was computed, and `Dossier.observe` compares this against the decision clock.
Each measured entry's deposition date, so the earliest can be checked rather than taken.

failures.symptom: no candidate structure could be measured
failures.cause: Returned, not raised: a target with no usable deposited structure is the ordinary case for a novel pathogen and the ranker has to keep working without one. The return carries the per-structure reasons and the chains that were offered, so an empty answer can be told apart from a broken one.

failures.symptom: None for an accession with no representative structure
failures.cause: `representative_structure` skips chains shorter than its floor, because a peptide fragment co-crystallised with something else has a surface but not the target's. An accession whose only entries are such fragments resolves to nothing.

geometry.surface_markers.citation: The pdb_id:chain pairs in `structures_used` and the freesasa version. A patch area with no structures named is not a cited claim, and the median without the spread is not the measurement.
geometry.surface_markers.warning: A surface marker is not an affinity, not a druggability score and not a prediction that any macrocycle binds. It is also computed on deposited conformations: the spread across structures of one domain reached a factor of six on haemagglutinin, so a single number from a single crystal is the error this tool is built to avoid reporting.

intake.rank_targets.name: intake.rank_targets
intake.rank_targets.summary: Pathogen genome accession to a ranked list of candidate binding targets.
intake.rank_targets.description: Six-frame ORF calling, homology identification against a reviewed UniProt reference, then a stated and unfitted ranking over conservation, surface exposure, essentiality and druggability features. Returns candidates with their features. It predicts no binding, affinity or inhibition for any of them, and the worth-binding score it reports is a separate axis from the confidence that the identification itself is correct.

parameters.name: accession
parameters.meaning: NCBI nucleotide accession for the genome to read.

parameters.name: exclude_organism
parameters.meaning: Organism removed from the reference before identifying, which scores a curated genome as if it were novel.

parameters.name: top
parameters.meaning: How many of the longest ORFs to identify.

parameters.name: remote
parameters.meaning: Whether identification may fall back to the remote aligner. The default local k-mer path is the one the recorded runs used.

parameters.name: record
parameters.meaning: Whether the function writes its own artifact. A call made inside an episode passes False, because the episode writes the record.

returns: Ranked candidate rows carrying score, conservation and tier.
The stated ranking weights, which are not fitted.
Host, commit and time, from common.provenance.

failures.symptom: A holdout that removes nothing raises rather than proceeding
failures.cause: `build_index(require_removal=True)` refuses an exclusion that matched no reference entry, because a holdout that silently removed nothing would report leakage as generalisation.

failures.symptom: The remote aligner reports a non-finished status
failures.cause: The EBI service queues; a 15-minute RUNNING queue is on the record as the reason the local k-mer path is the default.

intake.rank_targets.citation: Identification derives from the named reviewed UniProt release. A ranked target row is not a cited claim and cannot satisfy a dossier axis alone.
intake.rank_targets.warning: The worth-binding score and the identification confidence are different axes and must not be pooled. A high score resting on a hydropathy-only assignment is a row a reader has to be able to see.

literature.search.name: literature.search
literature.search.summary: Date-limited literature retrieval for a target name, protein family or accession.
literature.search.description: Queries Europe PMC's fielded search over title and abstract, optionally bounded by a publication-date ceiling, and returns hit counts by source and publication type together with the top hits and whether each carries an abstract. Europe PMC was chosen over NCBI E-utilities, OpenAlex, Crossref and Semantic Scholar on four measured criteria; the decisive one is that it indexes preprints and full text, returning 1173 hits where PubMed returned 25 on the same query, and at onset the preprints are the literature. A count is evidence of attention and of nothing else.

parameters.name: subject
parameters.meaning: The term, family accession or protein accession to query for.

parameters.name: subject_kind
parameters.meaning: Which kind of subject was supplied, which selects how the query is built.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.meaning: Which fields the query searches.

parameters.name: date_from
parameters.meaning: Inclusive ISO publication-date floor, or absent for no floor.

parameters.name: date_to
parameters.meaning: Inclusive ISO publication-date ceiling. The field that makes a hindsight audit falsifiable: without it a replay reads today's literature and reports it as what was knowable then.

parameters.name: top
parameters.meaning: How many hits to return in full.

parameters.name: per_axis
parameters.meaning: Whether to also run one narrowed count per dossier axis.

parameters.name: record
parameters.meaning: Whether the function writes its own artifact. An episode passes False.

returns: Total hits matching the query under the date bound.
The top hits, with identifiers, titles, dates and sources.
One narrowed hit count per dossier axis, when requested.
Hits split by index: MED, PMC, preprint, patent.
How many of the returned hits are preprints.
How many returned hits carry an abstract.

The control that proves the date bound was honoured: the clause, the hit count with and without it, and whether the two differ. Europe PMC discards an unparseable date clause silently and answers HTTP 200 with the unfiltered corpus, so a tool that trusted the status code would hand an auditor the wrong decade. Measured: 8244 hits unbounded against 4464 bounded.
Host, commit and time, from common.provenance.

failures.symptom: the date clause did not discriminate
failures.cause: Europe PMC echoes an unparseable date clause back and returns the unfiltered corpus at HTTP 200. The control query is run precisely so this is caught rather than trusted, and a non-discriminating clause is reported in `date_filter_verified` rather than silently accepted.

failures.symptom: urllib.error.HTTPError from the Europe PMC host
failures.cause: A public keyless endpoint with no declared rate limit. Observed as an HTTP error rather than a throttling response.

literature.search.citation: The hit identifiers and the exact query, including the date clause and the control counts. A hit count with no query is not a citable claim, and a count whose date clause was not verified is not a claim about any period.
literature.search.warning: A publication count measures attention, not truth. It cannot substantiate an axis on its own: a target with a thousand papers and no functional assay is still a target with no assay. Retrieving a paper and admitting its claim into a dossier are different operations, and only the first is implemented here.

similarity.homologs.name: similarity.homologs
similarity.homologs.summary: Homologs of one protein with identity, E-value and source organism.
similarity.homologs.description: Submits a sequence to EBI's HMMER phmmer service and returns the hits above an inclusion threshold, each with its percentage identity, E-value, source organism and domain architecture. HMMER was chosen after the endpoint this project had declared turned out to require an email address: EBI's job dispatcher answers HTTP 400 without one, so it is not an unauthenticated tool. HMMER needs no key and answered a 306-residue query against SwissProt in two seconds, where NCBI BLAST was still waiting past a minute.

parameters.name: query
parameters.meaning: An amino-acid sequence, or a nucleotide accession whose coding sequences are resolved first.

parameters.name: database
parameters.meaning: Which HMMER target database to search.

parameters.name: max_hits
parameters.meaning: How many hits to return.

parameters.name: min_identity
parameters.meaning: Percentage-identity floor below which a hit is dropped.

parameters.name: cds_index
parameters.meaning: Which coding sequence to use when the query was an accession.

parameters.name: max_wait_seconds
parameters.meaning: Ceiling on polling. Crossing it raises, because a timeout is a failure and not an empty hit list.

parameters.name: record
parameters.meaning: Whether the function writes its own artifact. An episode passes False.

returns: Homologs, each with accession, identity, E-value, organism and architecture.
Hits the service returned with no computable identity, counted rather than dropped: a hit with no identity cannot be filtered by one and must not silently vanish through the identity floor.
How many the identity floor removed, so the floor's effect is visible.

Names the best identity and says what it does not license. A homolog is somebody else's accession, and treating a low-identity hit as the query's own identity is the conflation this repository already warns about.
How many organisms the hits span.
How many architectures the hits span.
The release the search ran against.
Databases the service advertises and did not serve, recorded rather than retried.
Identity of the payload with timestamps stripped.
Host, commit and time, from common.provenance.

failures.symptom: the poll ceiling was crossed before the job finished
failures.cause: A job queue can stall. The ceiling raises rather than returning an empty hit list, because an empty list is a finding and a timeout is not.

failures.symptom: urllib.error.HTTPError from the EBI HMMER host
failures.cause: A public keyless endpoint. Observed as an HTTP error on submission or on result retrieval.

similarity.homologs.citation: The hit accessions with their identities and E-values, and the database release searched. A homolog name with no identity is not a cited claim.
similarity.homologs.warning: A homolog is another organism's protein. Its accession is not this target's identity, its annotation is not this target's annotation, and conservation measured across curated entries is not conservation across circulating strains.

structures.evidence.name: structures.evidence
structures.evidence.summary: Dated structural coverage per declared target, from PDBe and UniProt.
structures.evidence.description: For each target in the structures config, resolves the UniProt entry, the declared or derived residue ranges, and the PDBe entries covering them, then reports the earliest deposition date and best resolution. The structure count is a proxy for how much attention a target has received; it is not a pocket score, not a druggability estimate, and the two must never be pooled.

parameters.name: minimum
parameters.meaning: Fraction of a declared range a structure must cover to count.

parameters.name: record
parameters.meaning: Whether the function writes its own artifact. A call made inside an episode passes False, because the episode writes the record.

returns: Target name to a dated row carrying accession, structures, earliest_deposition, earliest_pdb, best_resolution, methods and pdb_ids.
The three endpoints and their licence terms.
Identity of the payload with volatile timestamps stripped.
Host, commit and time, from common.provenance.

failures.symptom: urllib.error.HTTPError from the PDBe or UniProt host
failures.cause: Both are public endpoints with no declared rate limit here, and the entry-summary call POSTs in batches of 400.

structures.evidence.citation: The UniProt accession and the PDBe entry identifiers covering the declared range. A count with no entry identifiers is not a cited claim.
structures.evidence.warning: A structure count is a research-attention proxy and a pocket score is not. They are different axes and must not be pooled. Coverage is computed per entry rather than per chain, because an obligate complex is two polymer entities and a per-chain test returns zero for every such structure ever deposited.

structures.folded.name: structures.folded
structures.folded.summary: Fold one amino-acid sequence with ESMFold, keyed on the sequence.
structures.folded.description: Submits a sequence to the ESM Atlas folding endpoint and returns the predicted coordinates, the per-residue confidence parsed from the B-factor column, and a neighbour-count burial proxy. This is the only structural lane whose input a genuinely unknown target can supply: every other one resolves an accession, and a novel protein has none, so they return a true and useless zero for the case this project is named for. ESMFold runs single-sequence with no alignment and no template.

parameters.name: sequence
parameters.meaning: Amino-acid sequence. A FASTA block is accepted and its header dropped.

parameters.name: target_name
parameters.meaning: A label carried into the record, or empty.

parameters.name: neighbour_cutoff
parameters.meaning: Radius in angstroms within which a beta-carbon counts as a neighbour for the burial proxy.

parameters.name: confident_plddt
parameters.meaning: Per-residue confidence at or above which a residue counts as confidently modelled.

parameters.name: record
parameters.meaning: Whether the function writes its own artifact. An episode passes False.

returns: Share of residues at or above the confidence threshold.
Contiguous stretches below the threshold, which usually mean disorder.
Per-residue neighbour counts. A contact number, labelled a proxy everywhere: no solvent model, no sidechain packing past the beta carbon, no probe radius. It is not solvent-accessible surface area.
Whether the returned coordinates align residue-for-residue with the sequence submitted.
Positions where they did not, which is how a silently truncated or reordered return is caught.
Why nothing was folded, when nothing was. An explicit recorded absence rather than an empty structure.
Identity of the payload with timestamps stripped.
Host, commit and time, from common.provenance.

failures.symptom: the folding endpoint returned no coordinates
failures.cause: The ESM Atlas service has been intermittently unavailable. Recorded as an explicit absence with the reason, rather than as an empty structure that would read downstream as a protein with no fold.

failures.symptom: the sequence exceeds what the endpoint accepts
failures.cause: The service bounds sequence length. A long polyprotein has to be split before folding, and the refusal says so rather than truncating silently.

structures.folded.citation: The sequence digest, the endpoint and the confidence vector. A fold with no sequence digest cannot be checked against the sequence it claims to be of.
structures.folded.warning: One monomer, one conformation, in vacuum: no partners, no glycans, no membrane, no ensemble. For a viral glycoprotein the biological unit is usually a trimer, so a surface scored here as exposed may be an oligomeric interface that is never solvent-exposed in the assembled particle. That is the precise question `accessibility` asks, answered wrongly, which is why this tool gates no axis.

structures.predicted.name: structures.predicted
structures.predicted.summary: Predicted structural models per accession, with per-range confidence.
structures.predicted.description: Inventories predicted models for a protein accession through the 3D-Beacons aggregator and retrieves per-residue confidence from AlphaFold DB, then summarises confidence over requested residue ranges. Both sources are needed and neither answers alone: AlphaFold DB reports a 404 and an empty body for an accession the aggregator shows a template-based model for, and the aggregator's residue endpoint silently covers one provider. Models marked experimentally determined are partitioned out and counted separately, never pooled into the predicted count.

parameters.name: accession
parameters.meaning: UniProt accession whose predicted models are inventoried.

parameters.name: residue_ranges
parameters.meaning: Residue intervals to summarise confidence over, or empty for the whole chain.

parameters.name: confident_plddt
parameters.meaning: Per-residue confidence at or above which a residue counts as confidently modelled.

parameters.name: residue_detail
parameters.meaning: Whether to return the full per-residue confidence vector.

parameters.name: record
parameters.meaning: Whether the function writes its own artifact. An episode passes False.

returns: Whether any predicted model was found. False is a finding: it means no modelling pipeline has covered this accession.
The predicted models, with provider, coverage and model-level quality.
Models the aggregator returned that are experimentally determined. Partitioned out rather than dropped, because a reader who sees models vanish deserves to know which tool owns them.
How many predicted models were found.
Per-requested-range confidence summary. A low-confidence stretch usually means disorder, which is a real finding about the site rather than a gap.
Requested ranges no model covers, kept apart from ranges a model covers badly.
Residue counts per confidence band, so a mean cannot hide a bimodal distribution.
Mean confidence per metric, because providers do not share one: AlphaFold reports pLDDT and SWISS-MODEL reports QMEANDisCo, and averaging across them would produce a number in no units at all.
When the most recent model was created.
When the earliest predicted model was created. This claim is knowable from that date and no earlier, which is what lets it enter a dated dossier.
Whether AlphaFold DB served anything for this accession, kept apart from whether a prediction exists at all.
Identity of the payload with timestamps stripped.
Host, commit and time, from common.provenance.

failures.symptom: urllib.error.HTTPError from the 3D-Beacons or AlphaFold host
failures.cause: Public keyless endpoints. A 404 from the AlphaFold prediction endpoint is recorded as that host serving nothing rather than as an absent prediction, because the two differ and the difference was measured on an accession this project already singles out.

structures.predicted.citation: The model identifiers with their providers and creation dates, and the confidence threshold applied. A confident fraction with no model identifiers is not a cited claim.
structures.predicted.warning: A predicted model is not a deposited one and must never be pooled into a structural count. It is also not evidence that the protein adopts that conformation: a confidence score is the model's confidence, not its accuracy, and it is least trustworthy on exactly the sparse-homology proteins this project cares about.
